title: Handle Late and Out-of-Order Events on Purpose
objective: Assign windows by event time, apply a documented allowed-lateness policy, and show in-window out-of-order events update the correct window while late events follow the written rule.
whyThisMatters: Processing time is when you saw the event. Event time is when it happened. Mixing them is how a 'daily total' moves after the day is closed and nobody can say whether that was policy or a bug.
evidence: The window size, event-time field, and allowed-lateness value in code or config
A captured event whose processing_time is in window B and event_time is in window A, landing in A
The late-event policy note and the fate of ten injected late events
Before and after measures for an out-of-order event inside allowed lateness
A closed-window measure that matches the written policy after a beyond-lateness event
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: Window assignment uses event_time, not processing_time, shown by an event whose processing_time is in window B but event_time is in window A landing in A.
All ten late events appear either as updates to their original window measures or as rows in a late_events table or file, and the chosen policy is named in a note.
An out-of-order event inside the allowed-lateness window is included in that window's measure, shown by captured before and after values.
An event beyond allowed lateness does not silently change a closed window unless the written policy says it does — the captured measure matches the policy.
